doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Piano heroes: Al Haig, John Lewis, Monk and Tristano
summary: Allison names pianists he admired as he arrived in New York.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: In New York at the time, $150 would be expensive for an unfurnished apartment. I’d like to speak a bit, if we can, about the development of your piano playing. We’ve spoken a lot about your devotion to bebop. You mentioned that you loved Al Haig...
John Lewis, yeah. I worshiped him from afar. He was with the Modern Jazz Quartet.
By the time you arrived in New York, the MJQ was in full swing. And he’d played with Dizzy Gillespie’s band, so you may have heard him on the road back in the ‘40s when you were in Mississippi.

Al Haig... You mentioned also George Wallington, who would help you, and Monk and Tristano. When you arrived in New York the second time, apart from the struggle of living in New York and raising a family, what was your impression of being there?
